name: oracle

attributes.attribute: a sign that divination reads to known the future
often misplaced in place or in season
marks bad, while an oracle stays neutral or fair
names a seer in the Greek classic use

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: An oracle is a mark or a turn that a divination rule reads to draw what follows. Such a system leans to signs to set the course of a thing. The sign may be the flight of birds, untimely clouds, or a bloom opening in the wrong season. Again and again the oracle sits shifted out of its own place, such as a shell lying on a summit or a tree flowering in winter. Some writers split the omen, which marks bad luck, from the oracle, which reads neither good nor ill. The word also names a seer, a use that is chiefly Greek, as at the Oracle of Delphi.

okr.objective: Separate the oracle, a sign or seer, from the omen while noting the Greek use of the word.
key_results: Oracles read the future by bird flight or by strange weather.
An oracle often appears driven out of its place or season.
An omen marks bad, while an oracle reads quiet or fair.
The Oracle at Delphi shows the Greek sense of the word.
